steps.t: Sites, remote users and cloud datacentres all connect through the nearest Cato PoP.
SPACE processes every flow once, with identity, device, application and risk context attached.
That one data set lands in the Cato Management Application: topology, analytics, events, stories.
XOps turns millions of raw events into correlated, MITRE-mapped incident stories.

steps.t: Site and policy definitions live in Git; a CI runner executes Terraform and catocli on merge.
The Cato GraphQL API, the same API the CMA runs on, applies the change with one audit entry per mutation.
New branch sites appear on the topology within minutes; policy reaches every PoP and every edge.
The eventsFeed API streams security and connectivity events into the SIEM continuously.

steps.t: The Cato Client on the device and the Socket at the site already supply the telemetry; no extra agents.
Device, Wi-Fi, LAN gateway, last mile, PoP and application are each scored Good, Fair or Poor.
The backbone carries the flow PoP to PoP, so Cato observes every hop the traffic actually takes.
Experience Monitoring shows the one failing segment; XOps anomaly stories raise it before users call.

Nothing blocked; one degraded segment. 7 nodes.

steps.t: MPLS, routers, firewalls, VPN head-ends, SWG, CASB/DLP and an SD-WAN overlay: seven families, seven consoles.
Every flow is inspected once at the nearest PoP; SD-WAN and the security service edge become one pass.
The backbone replaces MPLS, a Socket replaces router plus firewall, the Client replaces the VPN head-end.
Network and security are configured, monitored and audited in one console, the CMA.

steps.t: Every flow from every site, user and cloud already traverses a PoP, so XDR starts with full telemetry.
The single-pass engine inspects once; attack traffic is blocked at the PoP and its evidence recorded.
XDR correlates the signals into one ranked story queue, ML-scored and mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.
The analyst pivots story → events → fix in the same console; Cato MDR works the same queue 24×7.

steps.t: Scope workshop: success criteria are agreed and written down before anything is built.
Build the pilot: one branch Socket plus a remote cohort on the Cato Client, with the IdP syncing.
Test cycles work the register on the pilot's own traffic; evidence is captured weekly as it lands.
Wrap-up puts findings next to the criteria in a decision meeting booked at the workshop.

steps.t: Tracked policy hits, connections and detections from every edge become events at the PoP.
Data Lake units set the hourly peak: 2.5M events per hour each, licensed on the busiest hour.
Retained events are queryable in the CMA Events page for the 3, 6 or 12-month variant, then deleted.
Export to S3, Azure Blob, the eventsFeed API or a SIEM carries no additional Cato cost.

steps.t: PLCs, cameras, printers, medical devices and BYOD kit sit behind the Socket; none can run an agent.
The engine fingerprints each device from its own traffic: category, type, model, OS, manufacturer.
One live Device Inventory in the CMA spans every site; identification can take up to 12 hours.
The same attributes become device-attribute firewall rules, or sync to a CMDB via the GraphQL API.
